title: How an email gets delivered
description: From a composed message to your inbox: the message format, submission, server-to-server delivery, mailbox access, and the checks that stop forgery.
questions: what is the difference between smtp imap and pop3
how do spf dkim and dmarc work
what does a mime type do in email
how is email encrypted in transit

steps.title: Write the message
steps.subtitle: Message format and MIME
steps.description: An email is a block of header fields followed by a body. The message format defines the headers and MIME lets the body carry attachments and non-ASCII text.

steps.title: Hand it to your provider
steps.subtitle: Message submission
steps.description: Your mail app submits the message to your provider on a dedicated submission service, usually after authenticating, rather than sending directly to the recipient.

steps.title: Relay it to the recipient
steps.subtitle: SMTP
steps.description: Servers find the recipient domain's mail server and pass the message along with SMTP, hop by hop, until it reaches the destination mailbox.

steps.title: Read it from your inbox
steps.subtitle: POP3 and IMAP
steps.description: The mail you receive sits on a server until you fetch it. POP3 downloads messages and IMAP keeps them on the server and synchronizes folders and flags.

steps.title: Prove it is genuine
steps.subtitle: SPF, DKIM and DMARC
steps.description: Receivers check whether the sending server is allowed to use the domain, whether the message carries a valid signature from that domain, and what the domain owner wants done when a check fails.

steps.title: Protect it on the wire
steps.subtitle: Transport encryption
steps.description: Mail started out in cleartext. STARTTLS upgrades SMTP connections, current guidance prefers TLS from the first byte for submission and access, and MTA-STS lets a domain say that TLS is required.

rfcs.label: Use TLS for Email Submission and Access
